column1: # The site population: how many anomalies and signatures each security band
# holds at once, and how they cycle. Read by the server (`population::AUTHORED`,
# CP21); header frozen in docs/content/schema.md §4. Edit and restart.
# Spec: docs/content/C3-population.md §4.1 (table T1) and §6, plan §3.3.
# - key: the `site` delta's slot key (ruling 4). NEVER rename one (that drops
#   its live deltas); retire a row by deleting it and add a new key.
# - archetype: the client's dungeon archetypes, comma-separated (24 combat,
#   27 ore, 28 ice, 30 gas, 44 relic, 45 data) [V names, appConst].
# - count: live at once per system. A fraction is a per-system chance for one
#   more, seeded per system. Every count is [A].
# - difficulties: the client's 1-5 scan difficulty, or * for "the ore band of
#   this band" (C3 §7.2 rule R4). Mapping difficulty to a band is [I].
# - respawn_s: seconds after completion before the slot refills [A].
# - ttl_s: an unvisited live site expires at the first rollover after it [A].
# - The fw_* rows (W17 CP53b) hold the factional-warfare complexes (33-36,
#   appConst dunArchetypesFactionalWarfare [V]). The server keeps them to the
#   warzone systems and to complexes of that warzone's two militias
#   (`facwar::militias_by_system`), so they never appear elsewhere in low sec.
# Every row is [A] as a whole; `why` names what would falsify it.
key
column9: why

column1: # SOV-UPG-2 (#80): the sov threat-detection upgrades. A band written `sovupg:<exclusive
# group>:<tier>` is a null-space row that is live in a system only while the hub there
# has an Online upgrade of that exclusive group carrying that tier (`enables`
# `sites:<tier>` in content/sov/upgrades.tsv; `sov_upgrade::upgrade_online`). One tier
# is live at a time (the group is exclusive). Appended, so no earlier slot moves.
# [V] the six threat levels (minor and major, tiers 1-3): `sovereignty/upgrades/const.py:2624-2629`.
# [I] what a threat array spawns: the type's non-zero `attributeDistributionID*` of the
# system's pirate faction (ten per faction, dogma/const.py:307-376; else its universal
# list), read from the bundle at run time; the per-faction family is chosen by the system's
# pirate as the hub's server does (static_data_loader.py:64). [A] one live site per
# distribution id (falsifier: a TQ system with one array showing another steady number of
# its anomalies). So `band` = the upgrade, the live count = the type's distribution count
# (`sov_upgrade::distributions`), and `count` is only the reserve ceiling: 6, the old
# reserve, so no deployed world's floor anomalies change site id [A] (falsifier: a build
# whose arrays fill more than six slots; the live count is then clipped to 6). A type that
# names a family but none for this faction has no sites; a type with no distribution
# attribute at all uses the row's count [A] (falsifier: an owner wanting no sites without
# data).
# [V] tier = detection speed, not count: Minor arrays detect modest hostiles, Major the
# toughest, and arrays 2 and 3 detect new anomalies faster (client localisation text).
# [A] which dungeons: difficulty 1-3 for Minor, 4-5 for Major (falsifier: a TQ capture
# naming other sites). [A] the respawn seconds, falling with the tier inside a strength
# (falsifier: an owner balance ruling or TQ timing). Same-system placement only [A].
sovupg_threat_t1
column9: [A] a minor threat array tier 1 keeps one site per distribution it names and respawns each in 2400 s (the slowest of its strength) (client text: higher tiers detect new anomalies faster): falsified by an owner balance ruling or a TQ system showing other timings
